fixtureSet: HUMANITARIAN LANGUAGE QUALIFICATION R1 · the seven mandated cases, as data
note: Shared and importable. The spec RECOMPUTES every expectation through translationStateOf / qualifyText and never trusts a value in this file.

sourceShapes.reliefweb: metadata carries a `language` array; a record may declare several. Where it designates an original, that is `designatedOriginal`; where it does not, this product does NOT pick one.
sourceShapes.gdacs: metadata carries a language where available; where it is absent the field is absent, never defaulted.
sourceShapes.neverInferred: No case derives a language from a country, a region or a publisher's nationality. canonical already forbids it: NewsArticle.sourceLanguage is 'never fabricated or inferred'.

cases.why: Source language equals display language, so there is no translation and no translation label.
The answer may be Polish; the source was not. UNTRANSLATED is a displayable state and the citation must disclose the source language.

cases.mandated: English source -> PL answer, platform translated
cases.why: Labelled as a machine translation, and the source language is still disclosed. The original wording stays reachable.
A Polish source read in Polish is an original. The product must not label its own reader's language as a translation.
The mirror of T2b. Asymmetry here would mean the rule is English-centred.
No declared language, so no claim is sayable. Metadata is retained; the body is withheld rather than guessed.

cases.mandated: unknown language, and a translation exists anyway
cases.why: THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS. A translation of unknown origin must NOT be labelled PLATFORM_TRANSLATED — that would assert a source language by implication. UNKNOWN outranks every other branch.

cases.mandated: multilingual ReliefWeb record, no designated original
cases.why: Three declared languages and no designation. 'en' being among them does not make this text English — the product must not pick the one that suits the reader.

cases.mandated: multilingual ReliefWeb record WITH a designated original
cases.why: The source designated French as the original and published the English itself. SOURCE_TRANSLATION, and the source language is still disclosed because it differs from the answer.

cases.mandated: source translation vs platform translation — the same record, both routes
cases.why: Both are present. The SOURCE's own translation wins, and the platform's is not what the reader is told about. Precedence is the contract, not a preference.

cases.mandated: platform translation only, source supplied none
cases.why: NEGATIVE CONTROL for T6. The source translated into English, not Polish. A Polish reader must not be told the source translated this.

citation.originalTitle: Flash Update No. 3: Floods in Eastern Province

cases.why: A Polish answer citing an English OCHA update. The publisher name is not translated, the original title is carried, and the citation must state that the source was published in English.
Absence at the source is a different state from absence of a qualification, and gets its own reason and its own string.

cases.mandated: a source language outside the product's own language list
cases.why: `prs` is not a LanguageCode member and must not be coerced into one. It is carried verbatim and disclosed verbatim — canonical's own rule about a 'far larger set' than the UI list.

neverInferredControls.statement: No case supplies a country, and no function in the contract takes one. A country cannot reach a language decision because there is no parameter for it.
An empty declared list yields NOT_OBSERVED and UNKNOWN, never a guess from the publisher's nationality.
